item.title: [general] How AI Assistants are Moving the Security Goalposts
item.description: AI-based assistants or "agents" -- autonomous programs that have access to the user's computer, files, online services and can automate virtually any task -- are growing in popularity with developers and IT workers. But as so many eyebrow-raising headlines over the past few weeks have shown, these powerful and assertive new tools are rapidly shifting the security priorities for organizations, while blurring the lines between data and code, trusted co-worker and insider threat, ninja hacker and novice code jockey.

item.title: [general] Google study finds LLMs are embedded at every stage of abuse detection
item.description: <p>Online platforms are running large language models at every stage of LLM content moderation, from generating training data to auditing their own systems for bias. Researchers at Google mapped how this is happening across what the authors call the Abuse Detection Lifecycle, a four-stage framework covering labeling, detection, review and appeals, and auditing. Earlier moderation systems, built on models like BERT and RoBERTa fine-tuned on static hate-speech datasets, could identify explicit slurs with reasonable accuracy. &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/07/google-llm-content-moderation/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/07/google-llm-content-moderation/">Google study finds LLMs are embedded at every stage of abuse detection</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>

item.title: [general] Product showcase: Proton Authenticator is an end-to-end encrypted, open source 2FA app

It is available on Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android, allowing users to access their verification codes across devices. The app is designed to work without ads or tracking. item.title: [general] Windows Security app gets Secure Boot certificate status indicators as 2026 expiration approaches
item.description: <p>Microsoft&#8217;s Secure Boot certificates, issued in 2011, are approaching expiration in 2026. To help IT administrators track whether devices have received replacement certificates, Microsoft has added new status indicators to the Windows Security app, under Device security > Secure Boot. Updated 2023 certificates are being delivered automatically through Windows Update to consumer devices and some business devices. The new app indicators show whether a given device has received those updates, what its current certificate state &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/03/windows-secure-boot-certificate-update-2026-expiration/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/03/windows-secure-boot-certificate-update-2026-expiration/">Windows Security app gets Secure Boot certificate status indicators as 2026 expiration approaches</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>

[general] Apple’s Camera Indicator Lights
item.description: <p>A <a href="https://daringfireball.net/2026/03/apple_enclaves_neo_camera_indicator">thoughtful review</a> of Apple&#8217;s system to alert users that the camera is on. It&#8217;s really well-designed, and important in a world where malware could surreptitiously start recording.</p> <blockquote><p>The reason it&#8217;s tempting to think that a dedicated camera indicator light is more secure than an on-display indicator is the fact that hardware is generally more secure than software, because it&#8217;s harder to tamper with. With hardware, a dedicated hardware indicator light can be connected to the camera hardware such that if the camera is accessed, the light must turn on, with no way for software running on the device, no matter its privileges, to change that. With an indicator light that is rendered on the display, it&#8217;s not foolish to worry that malicious software, with sufficient privileges, could draw over the pixels on the display where the camera indicator is rendered, disguising that the camera is in use...</p></blockquote>
